# Results — Study 442 (Anchored VWAP)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **anchor a
VWAP to a significant event and the line becomes a price magnet that price respects** — tested
as an intraday event study on 5-minute bars. We anchor the VWAP to the **09:30 session open**,
detect every bar where price **crosses** the line, and measure the reversion-oriented reaction
over the next 1 / 3 / 6 / 12 bars (5–60 minutes) with a one-bar execution lag — then ask whether
the AVWAP is any more special than a **randomly placed** horizontal level. Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance **5-minute** OHLCV bars — 5 most-liquid US names (public, no key) |
| Basket | SPY, QQQ, AAPL, MSFT, NVDA |
| Window | **2026-03-30 → 2026-06-23** (As-of **2026-06-23**; the partial in-progress 2026-06-24 session is dropped) |
| Sessions / bars | **59** complete RTH sessions; **4,602** 5-minute bars per ticker |
| Anchor / event | AVWAP anchored to the **09:30 open**; event = a bar whose close crosses the line |
| Reaction / lag / costs | reversion-oriented forward return over 1/3/6/12 bars, **1-bar** entry lag (no look-ahead); **1 bp** one-way half-spread charged on **both** legs |
| Fingerprint | `36705730ed53` (sha1[:12] of the basket close columns) |

> **Short-span data limit (named on the Signal axis).** Yahoo serves only ~60 calendar days of
> 5-minute history, so this is a deliberately **short** window (59 sessions). The window is
> high-power *per day* (≈1,600 pooled touch events) but cannot speak to regime variation across
> years. We run it on the **most liquid** tape on purpose: tight spreads are the friendliest
> possible ground for an intraday level effect — if the magnet does not appear *here*, it appears
> nowhere. The reactions are tick-level (sub-basis-point), which is also a hard **capacity**
> caveat on the Tradability axis.

## The signal — post-touch reversion of the anchored VWAP (pooled basket)

Reaction signs are oriented so **positive = the level is respected** (a bounce: price reverts
back through the line) and **negative = price continues through it**. The *t* columns are the
one-sample / Newey-West (HAC) *t* of the reaction against 0; `t vs ctrl` is the Welch *t* of the
AVWAP reaction minus the random-level control.

| horizon | n touches | AVWAP reaction | random-level | HAC *t* | *t* vs control | win-rate | net of spread |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 bar  (5 min)  | 1,682 | +0.39 bp | +0.30 bp | +0.89 | +0.21 | 50% | **−1.61 bp** |
| 3 bars (15 min) | 1,662 | +0.25 bp | +0.49 bp | +0.45 | −0.33 | 51% | **−1.75 bp** |
| 6 bars (30 min) | 1,619 | +0.19 bp | +0.35 bp | +0.29 | −0.16 | 50% | **−1.81 bp** |
| 12 bars (60 min)| 1,545 | +0.41 bp | +0.95 bp | +0.50 | −0.36 | 51% | **−1.59 bp** |

Read it plainly. The post-touch reaction is a **fraction of a basis point** at every horizon
(0.01% = 1 bp), the **HAC *t* never exceeds 0.9** — nowhere near the desk's **t ≥ 2** bar — and
the win-rate is a **coin flip** (50–51%). The headline 6-bar one-sample *t* is **0.19**. There is
no statistically detectable magnet, on the most liquid tape there is.

## Is the line special? — the random-level placebo

The decisive test: a running VWAP is *an average*, so price crosses it constantly and "respects"
it trivially — exactly as it would a line drawn at random in the same range. We draw **2,000
random horizontal levels** per session and ask how often a random level's mean reaction matches
or beats the AVWAP's.

| metric (6-bar) | value |
|---|--:|
| AVWAP mean reaction | +0.19 bp |
| random-level control mean | +0.35 bp |
| **random-level placebo *p*** | **0.711** |

A random level reacts **at least as strongly as the AVWAP 71% of the time** — and on average
*more*. The AVWAP is **not** a special level; it is an average that sits in the middle of the
price and gets touched a lot.

## Costs — the spread is the executioner

Every touch is a fresh round trip (enter the next bar, exit `horizon` bars later). We sweep the
one-way half-spread; it is charged on **both** legs.

| half-spread (one-way) | gross (6-bar) | net |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.5 bp (best case, SPY) | +0.19 bp | **−0.81 bp** |
| 1.0 bp | +0.19 bp | **−1.81 bp** |
| 2.0 bp | +0.19 bp | **−3.81 bp** |

Even at the *tightest* assumption the trade is net-negative: the gross reaction is **thinner than
the spread** you must cross to capture it. This is the graveyard of intraday level trading.

## Per-name — no name carries it

| ticker | n touches (6-bar) | reaction | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY  | 358 | +0.81 bp | +1.16 |
| QQQ  | 316 | +0.80 bp | +0.70 |
| AAPL | 320 | −0.62 bp | −0.46 |
| MSFT | 295 | −1.22 bp | −0.69 |
| NVDA | 330 | +0.97 bp | +0.46 |

Random signs, every |*t*| under 1.2 — the fingerprint of noise, not a magnet hiding in a subset.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

On a deterministic intraday tape with a **planted** AVWAP magnet (a restoring pull of each bar's
return toward the running line), the post-touch detector behaves exactly as it must:

| planted magnet | n touches | reaction (6-bar) | one-sample *t* | HAC *t* | win-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no magnet) | 488 | +1.04 bp | +1.03 | +1.46 | 54% |
| **+0.10** (real planted magnet) | 745 | +2.23 bp | +3.39 | **+4.68** | 56% |

With **no** planted magnet the HAC *t* sits at 1.46 (it does not manufacture significance from
noise); a real planted magnet lights it up to **4.68**. The detector works — so the flat real-tape
result (HAC *t* = 0.29) is a genuine **"no,"** not a broken pipeline. *(Note: the random-level
placebo is a weaker discriminator in this control, because the global magnet lifts random levels
near the line too — the clean machinery proof is the HAC *t* on the AVWAP reaction.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The post-touch reversion is **+0.19 bp** at 6 bars (one-sample *t* = 0.19,
  HAC *t* = 0.29), flat across 1–12 bars, win-rate 50–51%, on the most liquid US tape. Nowhere
  near the **t ≥ 2** bar. Carries an explicit **short-span** caveat (59 sessions, ~60 days of
  5-minute history).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Net of a 1-bp half-spread × 2 legs the reaction is **−1.81 bp** at
  6 bars and negative at every cost level (−0.81 bp even at a 0.5-bp half-spread). The gross
  reaction is thinner than the spread; there is nothing to scale.
- **Price magnet? — NOT SUPPORTED.** A **random** horizontal level reacts just as strongly
  (control +0.35 bp vs AVWAP +0.19 bp; Welch *t* = −0.16) and matches/beats the AVWAP **71%** of
  the time (placebo *p* = 0.711). The anchored VWAP is an *average*, not a magnet — the
  convincing screenshots are selection (you remember the bounces, forget the pass-throughs).
